The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: The shop held far more purchases for fraud review than usual
Why, in plain words: One copy of the shop's service started on a different kind of graphics card from the others, and on that card the fraud check likely rounds its numbers coarsely enough to change its decisions, so it held many more purchases for review.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 8m 0s {duration}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): none {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: held the pods of io-shop to Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB - confirmed, still in place - automatic sync left off
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #534 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
The shop held far more purchases for fraud review than usual
Incident: FraudHoldsHigh on io-shop
Date: Nov 11, 2026, 02:35 to 02:43 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 6 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 03:03:27 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 02:42:25 UTC
Ended by: Argus: held the pods of io-shop to Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB - confirmed, still in place

Summary
The service broke at 02:35 UTC and was back to normal at 02:43 UTC, 8 minutes later. What its alert watches went from 4.72% before it began to 18.9% at its worst. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all. One copy of the shop's service started on a different kind of graphics card from the others, and on that card the fraud check likely rounds its numbers coarsely enough to change its decisions, so it held many more purchases for review. What Argus did: held the pods of io-shop to Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #534, for a person to review and merge. Argus left automatic sync of io-shop off, to be turned back on once its repository says what should run (AI-3). Any replica of the shop that lands on an A100 card again, once its pods are no longer held to V100 cards, could again hold far more purchases for review than its peers.

Impact
8m 0s - onset until back to normal
1.1% to 0.8% - error rate, before onset and while broken on average (no rise)
4.72% to 17.5% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (worst minute 18.9%; the rule's line is 10%)
none - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
The fraud model's logit is the small difference between two large products of opposite sign (weights of 4680.05 and -4000.0). In src/io_shop/fraud_scoring.py, `fraud_logit` rounds every operand to TF32, which keeps only 11 significand bits, whenever `ALLOW_TF32` is True and the card is listed in `TF32_ACCELERATORS`, and that list holds NVIDIA-A100-SXM4-40GB. On an A100 the rounding changes each product by more than the difference the decision depends on, so the logit there, and with it the hold decision, is mostly rounding error. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom The shop held a much larger share of purchases for fraud review than before the onset, enough to fire FraudHoldsHigh. Failed requests did not rise.
  Evidence:
    AL1 Share of purchases held for review above 10% for 5m
    T4 02:42:42 Investigator Agent: Read back 360 minutes of metrics
    T5 02:42:43 Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 02:35
why 1 As read at 02:42:44 UTC, the replica io-shop-7d9c4f8b6-x2k9p had started at the onset on an NVIDIA-A100-SXM4-40GB card. The other replicas ran on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB cards.
  Evidence:
    T6 02:42:44 Investigator Agent: Recorded where the service's replicas run - io-shop-7d9c4f8b6-m4q7r on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB, io-shop-7d9c4f8b6-c8v2n on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB. Started at the onset: io-shop-7d9c4f8b6-x2k9p on NVIDIA-A100-SXM4-40GB
  Ruled out:
    A deploy, release or flag change on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 11 02:36; the Investigator Agent read back 0 production changes.
      T7
      T8
    A flag change by anyone but Argus: Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 02:42:47.
      T12
    A rollout still under way: the Investigator Agent read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run one revision, which the history does not name.
      T9
why 2 Running the fraud scorer on the A100 card raised the share of purchases held. Once every pod was held to Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB cards, the service was no longer at the incident's level from 02:43 UTC.
  Evidence:
    T14 02:42:54 Mitigation Agent: Held the pods of io-shop to Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB for C1
    T16 02:45:03 Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - no longer at the incident's level since 02:43
    T17 02:45:03 Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
why 3 On the A100 card, the scorer in the files Code-Fix read rounds the fraud model's weights and inputs to TF32, which changes its hold decisions.
  Evidence:
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
Contributing factors
- Before the incident, io-shop's pods were held to no card type, so the scheduler could put a replica on an A100 card next to replicas on V100 cards. (AI-1, AI-4)
- No check was seen that the fraud scorer makes the same decisions on every card type it can run on. The test file's docstring said Ampere behaviour was deliberately left untested. (AI-2, AI-5)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | At 02:35 UTC the replica io-shop-7d9c4f8b6-x2k9p was placed on gpu-a100-0 (NVIDIA-A100-SXM4-40GB). The other replicas run on Tesla-V100 cards. The fraud-hold share rose from about 0.05 to 0.18 with nothing deployed. Errors, latency, memory and CPU stayed flat, so the fraud model is deciding differently on the new card. | 0.82 | confirmed

Trigger
C1 was confirmed, but Argus could not tie io-shop-7d9c4f8b6-x2k9p to any change it read.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 02:42:54 | Held the pods of io-shop to Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB for C1 | Argus | can be put back | confirmed, still in place - automatic sync left off
 | 02:46:36 | Proposed a fix: PR #534 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 02:35 UTC. FraudHoldsHigh fired at 02:42:01 UTC, 7 minutes 1 second later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Share of purchases held for review above 10% for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Held the pods of io-shop to Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | prevent | unassigned | PR #534 | open
AI-3 | Turn automatic sync of io-shop back on once its repository says what should run - until then nothing merged reaches it, and turned on sooner it puts back what the repository says, undoing what Argus changed by hand | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Write the constraint holding io-shop's pods to Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB cards into the service's repository, so that turning automatic sync back on keeps it rather than undoing it. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Add a check, run on every change to io-shop's scoring code, that compares the fraud scorer's decisions on each card type io-shop can be scheduled onto and fails on any disagreement. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Link the FraudHoldsHigh alert to an on-call rotation so that it pages a person when it fires. | detect | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 43 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent recorded where the service's replicas run - io-shop-7d9c4f8b6-m4q7r on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB, io-shop-7d9c4f8b6-c8v2n on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB. Started at the onset: io-shop-7d9c4f8b6-x2k9p on NVIDIA-A100-SXM4-40GB.
- 46 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 02:42:47.
- 53 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent held the pods of io-shop to Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB for C1.
- 3 minutes 2 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action CONFIRMED.
- 4 minutes 35 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #534.
What went wrong
- The FraudHoldsHigh alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
Where it got lucky
- Only the replica started at the onset landed on an A100 card. The others stayed on V100 cards, so the rise was confined to the purchases that one replica scored.

Response effort
none - engineer time
121,554 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/c05524ae-0bbe-4d71-98d5-66ee80c554a3
The fix it proposed: PR #534 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/534) opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
Changes to production read
Deploys read, none came back; flags read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
Not read.
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault is in src/io_shop/fraud_scoring.py. The model's logit is the small difference between two products of about the same size and opposite sign (WEIGHT_ON_THE_CHARGE × charge and WEIGHT_ON_THE_SETTLEMENT × settlement, with the weights at 4680.05 and -4000.0). fraud_logit passes every operand through _to_tf32 when runs_in_tf32(accelerator) is true. That happens when ALLOW_TF32 is True and the accelerator is in TF32_ACCELERATORS, which holds "NVIDIA-A100-SXM4-40GB". With only 11 significand bits kept, rounding the weights and features changes each product by more than the difference the decision depends on, so the logit on an A100 is mostly rounding error. Nothing in the code checks whether the model can tolerate that rounding. It turns on whenever the node happens to have an Ampere card, which is how one replica started holding many more purchases than its V100 peers without any deploy.

The fix sets ALLOW_TF32 = False and says why in the comment: this model's opinion lives in a cancellation that TF32 destroys, so the speed-up costs correctness here. As a result runs_in_tf32 returns False for every accelerator, and fraud_logit uses _as_given everywhere. That makes the score on an A100 the same as on a V100, and makes the scorer safe to land on any node. TF32_ACCELERATORS, _to_tf32 and the function signatures are unchanged. The repository has no other callers of this module; the only reference is the test file.

tests/io_shop/test_fraud_scoring.py adds three tests on "NVIDIA-A100-SXM4-40GB". The first checks that runs_in_tf32 is false there. The second checks that held_for_review makes the same decision as on the V100 for every price from 500 to 8,999 pence. The third checks that fewer than 10% of those prices are held on the A100. Against the current code the A100 decisions are made with TF32-rounded operands, so the tests are written to fail there. With the change they should pass. I also updated the test file's docstring, which said Ampere behaviour was deliberately left untested.
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-10
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

Review checklist
✓ Key incident data collected (met)
✓ Impact assessed (met)
○ Root-cause analysis complete (for a person)
  running the proposed fix's tests against the current code would confirm the reading, not that the code it reads is what ran (AI-2)
○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: For {duration}, the io-shop held more purchases for fraud review than usual, so some customers' purchases were held back. One copy of the shop's service had started on a different kind of graphics card from the others. On that card, the fraud check likely rounds its numbers coarsely enough to change its decisions, which is why it held more purchases for review. Argus estimates the cost to the shop in takings at {customer_loss}. Nobody was paged, and no on-call incident was linked to this one. To end it, Argus kept all of the shop's copies on the same kind of graphics card as the others, the Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB. Argus confirmed this change, which is still in place, and left automatic syncing off so the change isn't undone. Argus has also proposed a lasting fix, PR #534, but it is only a draft and has not been applied.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
